feat(CC-0115): default well-known ControlPlane infra/korc fields

Let a minimal managed-mode ControlPlane omit spec.infrastructure and
the spec.korc.adminCredential body: the defaulting webhook now fills the
well-known database, cache, and admin-credential references so callers
only need to supply openStackRelease and the services.keystone block.

- Add eight well-known defaulting constants to controlplane_webhook.go
  (database keystone / keystone-db / openstack-db, cache
  dogpile.cache.pymemcache / openstack-memcached, admin password
  keystone-admin with key password, cloud entry admin) as the single
  source of truth
- Materialize these defaults in the Default webhook for any zero-valued
  field, keeping the pass idempotent and never overwriting explicit
  values
- Guard the two managed clusterRef names (openstack-db,
  openstack-memcached) behind the brownfield discriminator: invent them
  only when database.host / cache.servers are unset, so the validating
  webhook's database/cache XOR still holds for brownfield CRs
- Default cloudCredentialsRef.cloudName to "admin" via both a
  +kubebuilder:default marker and the webhook, mark the field +optional,
  and drop it from the CRD's required list so the whole korc block can be
  omitted; regenerate the config and Helm CRD copies accordingly
- Keep the shared commonv1 leaves (DatabaseSpec, CacheSpec,
  SecretRefSpec) webhook-only with no +kubebuilder:default marker, since
  the keystone operator reuses those types and a c5c3-specific default
  would leak into its CRD
- Extend the webhook unit tests to assert the eight defaults on a bare
  CR, their idempotency, preservation of explicit values, that a
  brownfield host/servers CR is never coerced into managed mode, and
  that a present-but-empty clusterRef name is filled in place
- Add TestIntegration_MinimalManagedToReady driving the smallest valid
  ControlPlane (only openStackRelease + services.keystone) through every
  sub-reconciler to aggregate Ready=True, asserting the defaulted managed
  infra flows through to the projected Keystone CR's clusterRefs
- Refactor driveControlPlaneToAdminCredentialReady and the minimal CR
  helper to provision dependencies at the shared Default* constant names,
  so the same helper serves both the multi-CP and minimal-CR tests
- Update the controlplane-crd reference, quick-start guide, and the
  deploy/kind sample ControlPlane to show the minimal form alongside the
  fully-expanded equivalent, documenting the dual-layer vs webhook-only
  defaults and the operational contract that the operator consumes
  pre-seeded Secret content but never invents credential material
